accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) of the Reserve Bank of India?
o: The primary window for managing day-to-day liquidity through repo, reverse repo and SDF operations
A mechanism for determining the statutory liquidity ratio of banks
A facility exclusively meant for financing long-term infrastructure projects
A system for regulating foreign portfolio investment flows
accepted.x: LAF is the primary framework through which the RBI injects liquidity through repo and absorbs liquidity through reverse repo and SDF operations on a day-to-day basis.
accepted.tq: Identify the function of the monetary-policy facility rather than its institutional name.
accepted.sec: Liquidity management - LAF, SDF, fine-tuning operations, I-CRR, OMO, VRRR, sterilisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Standing Deposit Facility (SDF), introduced in April 2022, enables the Reserve Bank of India to
o: absorb surplus liquidity without providing collateral
lend long-term funds to commercial banks without collateral
purchase foreign currency from the public without issuing securities
finance the fiscal deficit directly through government securities
accepted.x: The SDF allows the RBI to absorb surplus liquidity without collateral. Therefore, the RBI need not hold government securities to drain funds through this facility.
accepted.tq: Test the distinctive feature of a closely related pair of liquidity facilities.
accepted.sec: Liquidity management - LAF, SDF, fine-tuning operations, I-CRR, OMO, VRRR, sterilisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF):
1. It was proposed by the Reserve Bank of India in 2015.
2. It was enabled through an amendment to the RBI Act associated with the Budget 2018-19.
3. It began operations in April 2022.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the SDF was proposed in 2015, enabled through the RBI Act amendment associated with Budget 2018-19, and operationalised in April 2022.
accepted.tq: Use a chronological cluster of institutional milestones and select the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Liquidity management - LAF, SDF, fine-tuning operations, I-CRR, OMO, VRRR, sterilisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In a variable-rate repo or reverse repo auction, the cut-off rate refers to
o: the rate fixed permanently by the Monetary Policy Committee
the first rate quoted by the Reserve Bank of India
the last accepted rate in the auction
the average bank rate during the financial year
accepted.x: In competitive VRR and VRRR auctions, the cut-off is the last accepted rate.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between an auction-determined rate and an administratively fixed policy rate.
accepted.sec: Liquidity management - LAF, SDF, fine-tuning operations, I-CRR, OMO, VRRR, sterilisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly distinguishes VRR from VRRR?
1. VRR injects liquidity into the banking system.
2. VRRR absorbs liquidity for maturities longer than the overnight SDF.
3. Both are auction-based instruments under the LAF framework.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: VRR injects liquidity, while VRRR absorbs surplus liquidity for longer maturities than the overnight SDF. Both operate as auction-based LAF tools.
accepted.tq: Split the options by matching each instrument with its direction and maturity characteristic.
accepted.sec: Liquidity management - LAF, SDF, fine-tuning operations, I-CRR, OMO, VRRR, sterilisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Fine-tuning operations of the Reserve Bank of India are primarily conducted to
o: keep system liquidity in line with the monetary policy stance
determine the annual financial statements of banks
fix the statutory floor for the SLR
replace all permanent open market operations
accepted.x: Fine-tuning operations, generally involving short-term VRR or VRRR auctions, are conducted to align liquidity conditions with the prevailing monetary policy stance.
accepted.tq: Match a specialised operational tool with its precise policy objective.
accepted.sec: Liquidity management - LAF, SDF, fine-tuning operations, I-CRR, OMO, VRRR, sterilisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: How many fine-tuning operations were conducted by the Reserve Bank of India during financial year 2024?
accepted.x: The RBI conducted 49 fine-tuning operations during FY2024.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise numerical figure using four closely spaced values.
accepted.sec: Liquidity management - LAF, SDF, fine-tuning operations, I-CRR, OMO, VRRR, sterilisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: On 10 August 2023, the Reserve Bank of India announced a temporary incremental Cash Reserve Ratio (I-CRR) of
accepted.x: The temporary I-CRR announced on 10 August 2023 was 10 per cent and was intended to absorb excess liquidity from the banking system.
accepted.tq: Test the exact percentage attached to a dated temporary policy measure.
accepted.sec: Liquidity management - LAF, SDF, fine-tuning operations, I-CRR, OMO, VRRR, sterilisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The temporary I-CRR announced in August 2023 impounded approximately how much liquidity from the banking system?
accepted.x: The temporary I-CRR impounded approximately ₹1.1 lakh crore from the banking system.
accepted.tq: Use the associated amount to distinguish a temporary reserve measure from ordinary CRR changes.
accepted.sec: Liquidity management - LAF, SDF, fine-tuning operations, I-CRR, OMO, VRRR, sterilisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to Open Market Operations (OMO) of the Reserve Bank of India, consider the following statements:
1. They involve outright purchase or sale of government securities.
2. They are used for managing durable liquidity.
3. They are conducted directly with the general public rather than through banks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: OMO involves outright purchase or sale of government securities for durable liquidity management. The operations are conducted through banks, not directly with the general public.
accepted.tq: Find the incorrect operational detail in an otherwise familiar definition.
accepted.sec: Liquidity management - LAF, SDF, fine-tuning operations, I-CRR, OMO, VRRR, sterilisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Market Stabilisation Scheme (MSS)?
o: It was introduced in April 2004 to sterilise excess liquidity created by foreign-exchange purchases
It replaces the repo mechanism for day-to-day liquidity adjustment
It was introduced in April 2004 to provide subsidised loans to exporters
It permits the Government to spend all proceeds from securities issued under the scheme
accepted.x: Under the MSS, introduced in April 2004, the RBI issues Treasury Bills and securities to absorb rupees created by foreign-exchange purchases. The proceeds are kept in a separate MSS account and cannot be spent by the Government.
accepted.tq: Use the purpose, date and restriction together to identify the correct scheme.
accepted.sec: Liquidity management - LAF, SDF, fine-tuning operations, I-CRR, OMO, VRRR, sterilisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The proceeds from securities issued under the Market Stabilisation Scheme are credited to
o: a separate MSS account which the Government cannot spend
the Contingency Fund of India for emergency expenditure
the Consolidated Fund of India for unrestricted expenditure
accepted.x: MSS proceeds are kept in a separate MSS account. The Government cannot use these proceeds for expenditure.
accepted.tq: Test the institutional destination and use-restriction of scheme proceeds.
accepted.sec: Liquidity management - LAF, SDF, fine-tuning operations, I-CRR, OMO, VRRR, sterilisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Long-Term Repo Operations (LTROs) introduced in 2020 provided funds to banks for a period of
o: one to three months at the reverse repo rate
five to ten years at the SDF rate
three to five years at the bank rate
one to three years at the repo rate
accepted.x: The LTROs introduced in 2020 provided one- to three-year funds to banks at the prevailing repo rate.
accepted.tq: Combine the maturity period with the applicable policy rate to avoid rate-maturity swaps.
accepted.sec: Liquidity management - LAF, SDF, fine-tuning operations, I-CRR, OMO, VRRR, sterilisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: On 4 September 2026, the Reserve Bank of India absorbed approximately ₹6.02 lakh crore through
o: an outright sale of foreign exchange reserves
accepted.x: The RBI absorbed about ₹6.02 lakh crore through two three-day VRRR auctions on 4 September 2026.
accepted.tq: Link a current numerical figure with the exact instrument and maturity.
accepted.sec: Liquidity management - LAF, SDF, fine-tuning operations, I-CRR, OMO, VRRR, sterilisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The surplus liquidity of approximately ₹10.32 lakh crore in September 2026 had the effect of
o: pushing the call rate below the repo rate
raising the SLR automatically above 40 per cent
pushing the call rate above the repo rate
reducing the repo rate to zero
accepted.x: The large surplus liquidity of about ₹10.32 lakh crore pushed the overnight call rate below the repo rate.
accepted.tq: Apply the relationship between excess liquidity and short-term market rates.
accepted.sec: Liquidity management - LAF, SDF, fine-tuning operations, I-CRR, OMO, VRRR, sterilisation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Quantitative tools — Margin requirements and moral suasion
Quantitative tools — Change the volume and cost of total credit
Qualitative tools — Direct the flow of credit among sectors or borrowers
accepted.x: Margin requirements and moral suasion are qualitative or selective tools. Quantitative tools include repo, reverse repo, OMO, CRR and SLR.
accepted.tq: Separate tools by whether they alter total credit or direct credit to selected borrowers.
accepted.sec: Quantitative vs qualitative tools - classification, most powerful tool  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is an example of a qualitative or selective credit-control instrument?
accepted.x: Margin requirement is a qualitative tool because it influences the direction and availability of credit against particular securities. OMO, CRR and SLR are quantitative tools.
accepted.tq: Identify the selective instrument among general credit-control measures.
accepted.sec: Quantitative vs qualitative tools - classification, most powerful tool  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A bank is allowed to lend ₹70 against a security valued at ₹100. If the margin requirement is raised, the immediate effect will generally be to
o: increase the value of the security automatically
convert the loan into an equity investment
reduce the loan available against the same security
increase the loan available against the same security
accepted.x: The margin is the gap between the value of the security and the loan. Raising the margin reduces the amount that can be borrowed against the same security.
accepted.tq: Apply the inverse relationship between margin requirements and credit availability.
accepted.sec: Quantitative vs qualitative tools - classification, most powerful tool  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a qualitative credit-control measure?
accepted.x: Variable reserve ratio, including CRR and SLR, is a quantitative or general credit-control instrument. Credit rationing, moral suasion and direct action are qualitative measures.
accepted.tq: Find the general tool placed among selective credit controls.
accepted.sec: Quantitative vs qualitative tools - classification, most powerful tool  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The policy repo rate is regarded as the main monetary-policy instrument because the Monetary Policy Committee sets it primarily to
o: achieve the inflation target and guide money-market rates
determine the annual SLR ceiling of 40 per cent
fix the exchange rate of the Indian rupee permanently
accepted.x: The MPC sets the policy repo rate to achieve the inflation target, while liquidity operations help keep money-market rates close to that rate.
accepted.tq: Connect the policy instrument with the objective it is designed to achieve.
accepted.sec: Quantitative vs qualitative tools - classification, most powerful tool  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following are eligible forms in which banks may maintain their Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)?
1. Cash held by the bank itself
2. Gold
3. Unencumbered Government securities and Treasury Bills
4. Approved securities
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: SLR may be maintained by banks themselves in cash, gold, unencumbered government securities including Treasury Bills and State Development Loans, and other approved securities.
accepted.tq: Check the complete list of eligible holdings rather than confusing SLR with deposits kept with the RBI.
accepted.sec: SLR - eligible forms of holding, statutory floor and ceiling  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes SLR from CRR?
o: SLR is maintained with the RBI, whereas CRR is held by the bank itself
SLR is held by the bank itself in specified liquid assets, whereas CRR is maintained as a cash balance with the RBI
Both SLR and CRR are maintained only in gold
Both SLR and CRR earn interest from the RBI
accepted.x: SLR consists of cash, gold and eligible unencumbered securities held by the bank itself. CRR is maintained as a cash balance with the RBI and does not earn interest.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two reserve ratios by place of holding and form of asset.
accepted.sec: SLR - eligible forms of holding, statutory floor and ceiling  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the statutory framework described for SLR, the permissible range as a proportion of Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL) is
accepted.x: The statutory range for SLR is 0 per cent to 40 per cent of NDTL.
accepted.tq: Recall both ends of the statutory range instead of only the prevailing level.
accepted.sec: SLR - eligible forms of holding, statutory floor and ceiling  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The earlier statutory floor of 25 per cent for SLR was removed by the
accepted.x: The Banking Regulation (Amendment) Act, 2007 removed the earlier 25 per cent statutory floor for SLR.
accepted.tq: Match the legislative amendment with the specific reserve-ratio change.
accepted.sec: SLR - eligible forms of holding, statutory floor and ceiling  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The SLR of scheduled commercial banks was approximately what percentage of NDTL in 1991-92?
accepted.x: The SLR stood at about 38.5 per cent of NDTL in 1991-92 and was subsequently reduced gradually.
accepted.tq: Use the historical level rather than the current SLR figure as the numerical clue.
accepted.sec: SLR - eligible forms of holding, statutory floor and ceiling  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The gradual reduction in the SLR from its 1991-92 level was undertaken on the advice of the
accepted.x: The SLR was gradually reduced after the recommendations of the Narasimham Committee on financial-sector reforms.
accepted.tq: Use the committee-recommendation trap by matching the reform with the correct committee.
accepted.sec: SLR - eligible forms of holding, statutory floor and ceiling  [APPSC]

accepted.s: If a bank fails to maintain the required SLR, the penalty is generally charged at
o: the bank rate plus 3 per cent, rising to bank rate plus 5 per cent if the shortfall continues
a fixed rate of 5 per cent without reference to the bank rate
the repo rate plus 1 per cent, irrespective of duration
the bank rate minus 3 per cent, rising to bank rate minus 5 per cent
accepted.x: The penalty for an SLR shortfall is bank rate plus 3 per cent per annum, rising to bank rate plus 5 per cent when the shortfall continues.
accepted.tq: Watch for reversed plus-or-minus comparisons and the continuing-shortfall condition.
accepted.sec: SLR - eligible forms of holding, statutory floor and ceiling  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding securities issued under the Market Stabilisation Scheme is correct in relation to SLR?
o: They can be held only by the RBI and not by banks
They are expressly excluded from SLR computation
They count towards the SLR of banks
They count only towards CRR and not SLR
accepted.x: Market Stabilisation Scheme securities are eligible to count towards the SLR maintained by banks.
accepted.tq: Test whether a named government security qualifies for the specific reserve requirement.
accepted.sec: SLR - eligible forms of holding, statutory floor and ceiling  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following statements about CRR and SLR is correct?
1. CRR is governed by Section 42 of the RBI Act.
2. SLR is governed by Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
3. Banks earn interest on their CRR balances with the RBI.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: CRR is governed by Section 42 of the RBI Act and SLR by Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949. CRR balances do not earn interest, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Combine legal provisions with the interest distinction to eliminate the false statement.
accepted.sec: SLR - eligible forms of holding, statutory floor and ceiling  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: CRR — Cash, gold and unencumbered securities held by the bank itself
SLR — Cash balance maintained with the RBI
CRR — No interest is paid on the required balance
SLR — Governed by Section 42 of the RBI Act
accepted.x: No interest is paid on the CRR balance maintained with the RBI. SLR consists of specified liquid assets held by the bank itself and is governed by Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure pair and reject options that swap CRR and SLR features.
accepted.sec: SLR - eligible forms of holding, statutory floor and ceiling  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Proposal of the Standing Deposit Facility by the RBI
B. Enabling of the SDF through the amendment associated with Budget 2018-19
C. Introduction of LTROs
D. Commencement of the SDF
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The SDF was proposed in 2015, enabled in connection with Budget 2018-19, LTROs were introduced in 2020, and the SDF began in April 2022.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last milestones, then place the intervening policy developments.
accepted.sec: Liquidity management - LAF, SDF, fine-tuning operations, I-CRR, OMO, VRRR, sterilisation  [APPSC]
